tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. Their 0.5mm and 0.3mm scribing needles are perfect for scale models. Hold the tool at a 45-degree angle and apply gentle pressure while moving along the panel line. Start from one end of the line to avoid damaging the surface. Use the wider needle for deeper lines and the finer one for details. For larger lines, consider using their 1mm needle.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki tape
tips.text: Both Tamiya tape and Kabuki tape are suitable for masking, but they have different uses. Tamiya tape is easier to use and adheres well to most surfaces, making it ideal for simple shapes and curved surfaces. Kabuki tape, however, is more conformable and stickier, making it perfect for complex curves and intricate shapes. For best results, use Tamiya tape for general masking and Kabuki tape for complex shapes.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Brush Guards
tips.text: To keep your Iwata airbrush needle clean and functioning smoothly, use Iwata brush guards for cleaning. After each painting session, remove the needle and wash it thoroughly with warm water and mild detergent. Then, scrub it gently with a soft brush and the brush guard to remove any dried paint. Rinse and dry the needle before reinserting it into the airbrush.

tips.title: Scratch-Building with Evergreen Styrene Sheet
tips.text: Evergreen styrene sheet is versatile for scratch-building. To make a curve, cut the sheet into strips, then soak it in warm water for 10-15 seconds. Bend the strip gently into the desired shape while it's wet. Let it dry completely in the shape. For complex curves, use multiple strips layered together. Use CA glue to attach parts and sand with fine grit sandpaper once dry.

tips.title: Using Dental Tools for Detail Work
tips.text: Dental tools are invaluable for scale model detail work. For instance, use a dental probe (e.g., from a dental pick-up set) to create tiny holes or indentations. Gently push the probe into the surface, applying steady pressure. For removing small amounts of material, use a dental explorer to carefully scrape away excess plastic. Be cautious not to apply too much pressure and damage the model.
